name: Inquiry
rows: HANGS General Contracting LP
Inquiry
Quarter ended September 30, 2026 · USD · Quarterly review workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · review procedures, not an audit · not a review report · no conclusion expressed
Question
Status
Corroborated by
Answer, from the controller’s written responses
Q1 Revenue. Why is contract revenue higher than last quarter and than the budget?
Corroborated
Revenue rebuilt from the jobs agrees with the books

Pier 9 Lofts was at full framing crews all quarter and Alder Point moved into interior work. Rainier Commons and Weller Street started in the quarter. Revenue is the job schedule: costs to date against estimated total costs on every job. Subcontractor costs rose with the work, so payables and the retainage we hold back from subcontractors rose too.
Q2 Billings. Why did the job schedule move from billings ahead of revenue at June 30 to revenue ahead of billings at September 30?
Partly corroborated (REV-01)
The swing is explained; PCO-14 is unsigned

Mostly Alder Point. Its estimate now includes pending change order PCO-14 for the MRI suite shielding redesign, $640,000, which we priced and submitted on August 28. The owner’s architect has reviewed the pricing and we expect the owner to sign it in November. We cannot bill it until it is signed.
Q3 Margins. Why is the gross margin lower than last quarter and the budget?
Corroborated (JOB-01)
The schedule shows the same revised estimate

Tideflats Cold Storage. In August we found cracks in tilt-up wall panels and 14 panels are being recast, and our insulated metal panel supplier raised its price 9%. We revised the estimate at September 30 from $16,284,000 to $17,480,000. We have a backcharge claim against the panel precaster that we have not recorded. The job is still profitable. No other job’s estimate changed by more than a rounding amount.
Q4 Accrued wages. Why did accrued wages nearly double since June 30?
Corroborated
The payroll ledger’s accrual journals
The September 30 accrual covers wages earned September 14 to 30, paid on October 2 and October 16. At June 30 the accrual covered only June 22 to 30.
Q5 Interest. How is interest on the Cinderbrook loans recorded?
Contradicted (INQ-01)
The bank’s statement and the books: September is not accrued
Interest on both Cinderbrook loans is accrued monthly. The bank debits it on the first of the following month.
Q6 Cash and the line. Why is cash lower and the line of credit higher than at June 30?
Corroborated
The August 14 advance on the bank’s statement

We drew $1,200,000 on the line on August 14 to pay subcontractors on Pier 9 while two owner payments were late. Receivables are up because September billings were larger and Juniper Row’s September billing was still open at quarter end.
Q7 Related parties. Do you have any transactions with related parties?
Corroborated; no note (RP-01)
Account 1210 and job J-2625
Juniper Row Homes is built for HANGS Construction Development LP, which has the same owners as HGC. It is billed on the same terms as other owners.
Q8 Accounting changes. Did any accounting policy or estimate method change in the quarter?
Recorded
Same method on both schedules
No. We use the same cost-to-cost method and the same change order policy as at June 30.
Q9 Subsequent events. Has anything happened since September 30 that could affect the statements?
Recorded (SUB-01)
After the quarter
On October 9 we drew another $500,000 on the line. Lakeside Clinic started in October and was first billed on October 30.
Q10 Claims and litigation. Are there any claims, disputes or lawsuits by or against the partnership?
Recorded
No claim in the records
Only our backcharge claim against the Tideflats panel precaster. No owner has made a claim against us.
Q11 Covenants. Was the partnership in compliance with the Cinderbrook covenants at September 30?
Tested (COV-01)
Met, with little net worth headroom
Yes. Our compliance certificate goes to the bank by November 14, 2026.
Q12 Fraud and going concern. Do you know of any fraud or suspected fraud, or any doubt about the partnership continuing as a going concern?
Recorded
Nothing in the records says otherwise
No to both.
Answered in writing by Dana Whitfield, Controller, on October 26, 2026. Written answers are not a representation letter (REP-01).
